steps.content:
June 23, N.F. 115
10:24 AM

Refugee Settlement, Outside the Aurum Secretum Institute

A cold morning mist clings to the refugee camp. Beneath the frayed tents, people huddle together, their silence thick with exhaustion. The air reeks of filth and decay—even the wind seems burdened, carrying the stale breath of sickness and despair. Until...
In the distance, a lone figure glides across the mud-choked path, pristine white against the grime.

steps.speaker: Enthusiastic Refugee
steps.content: He's here!
The camp erupts. A surge of bodies presses forward, voices rising in desperate hope as they swarm around Saffar.

steps.speaker: Enthusiastic Refugee
steps.content: Look at me, Saffar! See, I've caught Mania already. It's finally my turn now, right?

steps.speaker: Anxious Refugee
steps.content: No, no, pick me! Look at my arm, it's way worse than hers, totally rotten! I might even turn into a Sinner any day now. C'mon, take me instead!
At the far end of the bustling crowd, Hella lingers in disguise, her sharp eyes fixed on the scene before her.
She recognizes the man. He was there at yesterday's welcome ceremony when she first arrived at the institute. One of their own.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ...Hey, what's going on here? What... are they doing?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Oh right, you just got here. You probably don't know about this yet.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: This is one of the ways to get into the institute, a regular screening that happens once every two months.
Thani's tone is effortless, as if this were the most ordinary thing in the world.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: That man over there in the middle is <color=#fb9259>Saffar</color>, the screening officer from the research institute. He comes here regularly to pick up people who are really sick and take them for treatment.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Oh yeah! The folks who came from Furor yesterday? He took them too... Are you worried about them? Aw, don't be! The institute's technology is really advanced. They'll get better in no time!
Treating refugees? Since when have the Fraser people played philanthropist?

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Would they really be that excited just for "treatment"? No... they want something else...
Hella scans the crowd again. Amid the shoving and jostling, a tattered cloak is torn away, exposing a twisted, broken body beneath—the unmistakable marks of Mania's corruption.
Yet no fear flickers in the faces around her. Only feverish devotion, a hunger burning in their eyes.
She knows that look. It's the same desperate gaze the Syndicans once fixed upon the other side.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: They all want to become Aurum Secretum Warriors?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Hehe... Well... How should I put this...

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: There's never enough food and medicine to go around. They... just want a better life.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: For everyone here, getting infected means a chance to become a Sinner, a chance to get into Fraser...

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: Like Synex?

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: ...If there's one Synex, of course there can be a second Synex.
Thani points toward the center of the crowd.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Just like Saffar there. He's also someone who made it out of this place.
Hella looks toward the figure in the center of the crowd.

Saffar listens patiently to everyone's concerns, his tone gentle and his movements deliberate, without a hint of impatience. Even when faced with deformities and disabilities, his expression never wavers. Instead, he bends down to meet the refugees at eye level, treating them with unwavering dignity.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: ...Would someone like that really be willing to come back here?
It's like seeing a Syndican who ran off to Eastside, only to return a few days later, complaining they "just couldn't get used to it there."

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Saffar is a kind person. The elders always tell me that out of all the kids who left, Saffar's the only one who still comes back to check on everyone...

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: And sometimes he even brings extra medicine and stuff. It's because of him that things aren't as tough around here.

steps.speaker: Hella
steps.content: What about the others who made it into the institute? Has no one else ever come back?
Thani offers a bitter smile.

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: Hehe... I guess after they got better, they just ended up staying in Fraser. Can't really blame them, though. Everyone's had enough tough times around here...

steps.speaker: Thani
steps.content: After all... where else could we possibly go?
Suddenly, shouts of surprise erupt from the excited crowd. A middle-aged woman rushes to Saffar, her voice trembling with desperation.

steps.speaker: Sandra
steps.content: Sir! Please, I beg you, tell me about my boy... How's he doing?

steps.speaker: Sandra
steps.content: My boy... You picked my boy...!

steps.speaker: Saffar
steps.content: You are...

steps.speaker: Sandra
steps.content: My poor little Yuri... Is he doing all right now? Has he recovered? I-I...
The woman's voice trembles, her hands shaking so violently she can barely clutch Saffar's robe.
Some agitated refugees try to pull the woman away, only to be halted by Saffar. Deliberately, he crouches to her level, steadying her with firm yet gentle hands.

steps.speaker: Saffar
steps.content: I remember him. He was such a lively child... yet Mania tortured him to the brink of death...

steps.speaker: Saffar
steps.content: He's... fine now. And all of us will be fine, too.
Saffar stands up, his voice resonating throughout the crowd.

steps.speaker: Saffar
steps.content: The Farland Alliance is facing a crisis. Calamities spread chaos, monsters rampage through the streets, and DisCity keeps restricting our access to Hypercubes... We have suffered loss after loss, powerless to fight back.

steps.speaker: Saffar
steps.content: We need strength—desperately. And we must stand together.

steps.speaker: Saffar
steps.content: Do not fear Mania! Calamities won't destroy us. Challenge it. Harness it. And in return, we'll be granted extraordinary power—
With a deliberate motion, he raises his palm. The Aurum Secretum coiled around his wrist pulses to life, emitting a soft glow. The crowd stirs with admiration, their awed voices rising like a tide.

steps.speaker: Saffar
steps.content: My friends, the earth beneath us is scarred with countless wounds, and the sky above has long been choked by dark clouds. But never forget, no matter how long the night, dawn will always come!

steps.speaker: Saffar
steps.content: The Great Expo delegation has already left Fraser. They'll bring Aurum Secretum to counter DisCity's grip. As long as we hold onto patience and hope...
He takes Sandra's hand and speaks with firm conviction.

steps.speaker: Saffar
steps.content: Everyone will find salvation. I'm certain of it.
[Fade Out to Switch Scene: Same Background]
Hella stands silent, struck by the bitter familiarity of it all. She had heard similar words in Syndicate, more than once.
"Power," "hope," "stand together"... such familiar terms. The farland refugees lean in, starved for meaning, but all she hears is Rustfire's shackles, polished and repackaged.
Liar...
Why is it that no matter where I go, people keep falling for these stupid, empty promises...
The screening process draws to a close. Rejected refugees scatter like autumn leaves while the chosen few coalesce into an orderly line.
Hella's gaze lingers on the long queue, and an idea begins to take root in her mind.
